summary_bullets: The S1 model is DuplexOmni, with S2 disabled; Moshi and MiniCPM have not run in this pilot.
Empty fields, quiet-input sensitivity, response-format rejection and waiting for disabled S2 are separate observed failures.
Gain and prompt changes elicit speech, but their combined condition gives 0/3 complete source-supported spoken answers.
findings: The empty P01 control is generated by the S1 language model itself: 41 valid responses have empty speech text, before the speech backend runs.
Question level changes recognition: the quiet native-packet questions are missed or misheard, while louder versions recover more of the request; this does not by itself recover the meeting facts.
The folder request triggers [THINK] in native-packet mode, so S1 waits for the deliberately disabled S2; the acknowledgement is not a completed lookup.

The correct plain-text answer from the earlier A100 run was lost at the caller’s format check, not at the audio encoder; generic format instructions reduce that interface failure but do not guarantee correct content.
The combined direct-answer prompt and gain produce spoken answers on all three questions, but all three miss or contradict required facts; silence reduction is not an accuracy fix.
Question-only buffered controls can also be silent, so these failures cannot be attributed to long meeting history alone.

Supplying the exact question text fixes the ambiguity answer in one ordinary-text control, while a full transcript still leaves unsupported status claims; both audio understanding and grounding need qualification.
audit.scope: These are caller/behavior diagnostics on three existing questions, not results for the full105 benchmark. Oracle text outputs are not native S1 speech baseline results. No model weights or question texts were changed.
audit.software_fixture: Suffixed diagnostic IDs now use an explicit progress index; a CPU HTTP/output fixture passed before the corrected speech run.
audit.speech_delivery_finding: Some independent transcripts contain request-like words or differ from native tts; whether this reflects speech generation or ASR errors still needs listening, and printed tts alone does not certify the spoken answer.
remaining: Separate native S1 behavior from an explicit answer-now content control before interpreting silence as reasoning or memory failure.
Separate native S1 behavior from an explicit answer-now content control before interpreting silence as reasoning or memory failure.
Keep output-format errors, native empty fields, S2-waiting and ASR uncertainty separate in evaluation records.
Qualify native packet input and buffered answer-text modes separately; neither is established as a reliable long-meeting spoken-answer baseline.
Use the same source-grounded scoring contract to qualify Moshi and MiniCPM before full-bank runs; further prompt selection belongs on separate development meetings.
